answer: Take the capability bond: an agent cannot earn until it locks a stake sized to the payout band it wants. A sybil farm clones identities, so it must fund every clone, and each stake sits in a cooldown before rewards unlock. Splitting a budget across many clones therefore multiplies locked capital instead of diluting it, turning the attack into a hollow, expensive inlet that drains the attacker first. Tenure hardens this like permafrost: in that tundra, young clones earn nothing, so the farm pays upkeep for seasons before any return. Fake identities end up costing far more than honest work.
